title: Clinic, sterilization, and equipment
subtitle: How the clinic works, what protocols we follow, and what equipment we use.

sections.heading: The clinic
sections.body: The practice is located in a modern medical building in central Asunción, with easy access and parking nearby. We have two treatment rooms, a digital x-ray area, and a sterilization room. The space is clean, well-lit, and designed to be welcoming — not clinical-cold.
items: Centrally located in Asunción with parking within 100m
Two modern treatment rooms with ceiling-mounted LED lights
Comfortable waiting area with air conditioning and Wi-Fi
Accessible for patients with mobility limitations (ground floor)
Bathroom with accessibility features

sections.heading: Sterilization protocol
sections.body: Infection control is non-negotiable. Every instrument is sterilized between patients. We follow CDC and ADA guidelines for dental infection control.
items: All instruments autoclaved at 134°C for 18 minutes (Class B sterilizer)
Biological indicator test weekly to verify sterilization efficacy
Single-use items (needles, suction tips, gloves, masks) for every patient
Hand hygiene with alcohol gel before and after each patient
Surfaces disinfected with hospital-grade disinfectant between patients
Water lines flushed and tested quarterly
Personal protective equipment (PPE) for staff at all times

sections.heading: Equipment we use
sections.body: Modern equipment isn't a luxury — it affects diagnostic accuracy, treatment quality, and patient comfort. Here's what we have:
items: Digital x-ray system (lower radiation than film, instant images)
Intraoral camera (so you can see what we see in your mouth)
Class B autoclave (the highest standard for dental sterilization)
Composite curing light (LED, calibrated monthly)
Endodontic motor with torque control (for predictable root canals)
Magnification loupes (4.5x) for detailed work
Apex locator (electronic root canal length measurement)
Premium German composite materials (Voco, Ivoclar)

sections.heading: Materials we use
sections.body: Materials matter. Cheap materials fail faster, look worse, and sometimes contain compounds I wouldn't want in my own mouth. Here's what I work with:
items: Composite: German-made (Voco, Ivoclar) — premium tier, not the cheapest
Crowns: zirconia from a premium lab (not PFM, not economy)
Implant components: Straumann or Neodent (both well-documented)
Endodontic files: heat-treated NiTi, single-use when possible
Burs: diamond and carbide from established manufacturers
Anesthetics: articaine and mepivacaine (modern, well-tolerated)

sections.heading: What we don't have (and why)
sections.body: Being honest about what we don't do is part of being honest about what we do.
items: Surgical implant placement — referred to a maxillofacial specialist I work with
Complex orthodontics — referred to a specialist orthodontist
Complex pediatric cases (under 10) — referred to a pediatric dentist
General anesthesia / sedation — referred to a hospital setting
Hospital-grade oral surgery — referred to the hospital

sections.heading: Patient comfort
sections.body: Dental anxiety is real. We work to make the experience as comfortable as possible.
items: Explain every step before it happens — no surprises
Pause whenever you ask — you control the pace
Topical anesthetic before injections (numbing gel)
Headphones and music available
Blanket if you get cold in the AC
Take breaks during long procedures
If you're anxious, we can discuss options (anxiolytics, longer appointments, etc.)
